correctness.rationale: The source equilibrium relation reduces to \(q=G_R(z)=\log z/[z(1-z/R)]\), \(1<z<R\). The derivative has the sign of \(N_R(z)=1-z/R-(1-2z/R)\log z\). Since \(z(1+2\log z)\) is strictly increasing, \(N_R\) has one minimum; at that point its value is \(L(3-2L)/(1+2L)\), so the exact transition is \(L=3/2\), or \(R=4e^{3/2}\). Endpoint signs then give zero or two critical points and the complete horizontal-line root count. Direct differentiation of the active subsystem gives the stated determinant-slope identity. The inspected verifier reproduces the cusp constants, fold levels, three-root example, active-region check, and determinant signs; the all-parameter classification is analytic.

value.rationale: The exact cusp threshold organizes the full endemic-equilibrium phase diagram of a recently published nonlinear media model, and the determinant-slope identity immediately identifies the middle branch as a saddle. This is a natural structural classification with direct relevance to the model's bistability regime.
residual_risks: The theorem is local/equilibrium-level and does not by itself establish global bistability.

final_claim: For the active-media endemic-equilibrium equation in the Wang--Yang--Yang SIR model, the exact universal cusp threshold is \(R_c=4e^{3/2}\): below it every \(q>0\) gives one endemic equilibrium, above it the model has the stated one/two/three/two/one root diagram between two folds, whose cusp is \((4e^{3/2},2e^{-3/2})\); moreover the Jacobian determinant has the sign of \(G_R'(z)\), so the middle branch is always a saddle.
limitations: The theorem classifies endemic equilibria in the active-media region only.
It does not prove global bistability throughout the three-equilibrium wedge or classify Hopf bifurcations of the outer branches.
